question: How is the height of a planer gauge adjusted?
solution:
```html

**Concept**

 
• A planer gauge (also known as a planer and shaper gauge) is a precision tool used primarily in machine shops for setting cutting tools on planers and shapers, as well as for layout work.
 
• It consists of a base with an inclined guide and a sliding block that moves along this incline.
 
• As the sliding block moves along the inclined plane, its vertical height relative to the base changes.
 
• To achieve high precision, these gauges incorporate a fine adjustment mechanism.

**Adjustment Mechanism**

The adjustment of a planer gauge involves two main steps:

 
• **Coarse Adjustment:** The sliding block is moved manually along the inclined track of the base to reach an approximate height.
